ref: 1 Apol. 6.1-2 (Otto section 6; ANF ch. VI 'Charge of atheism refuted')
greek: 6. Ἐνθένδε καὶ ἄθεοι κεκλήμεθα. Καὶ ὁμολογοῦμεν τῶν τοιούτων νομιζομένων θεῶν ἄθεοι εἶναι, ἀλλ᾽ οὐχὶ τοῦ ἀληθεστάτου καὶ πατρὸς δικαιοσύνης καὶ σωφροσύνης καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἀρετῶν, ἀνεπιμίκτου τε κακίας θεοῦ· ἀλλ᾽ ἐκεῖνόν τε, καὶ τὸν παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ υἱὸν ἐλθόντα καὶ διδάξαντα ἡμᾶς ταῦτα, καὶ τὸν τῶν ἄλλων ἑπομένων καὶ ἐξομοιουμένων ἀγαθῶν ἀγγέλων στρατὸν, Πνεῦμά τε τὸ προφητικὸν σεβόμεθα
greek_edition: S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.T. Otto, vol. 1, Jena: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1): text through 'καὶ τὸν τῶν' read on the page image, PDF p.228 = printed p.148 (image checked). Remainder 'ἄλλων ἑπομένων ... σεβόμεθα' from Migne PG 6 OCR (not on image checked).
english: Hence are we called atheists. And we confess that we are atheists, so far as gods of this sort are concerned, but not with respect to the most true God, the Father of righteousness and temperance and the other virtues, who is free from all impurity. But both Him, and the Son (who came forth from Him and taught us these things, and the host of the other good angels who follow and are made like to Him), and the prophetic Spirit, we worship and adore
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1)
page: ANF printed p.164 (PDF p.182, offset +18, inferred); Otto printed p.148 (PDF 228, offset +80, verified on image)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (1885-96), ed. Roberts & Donaldson; archive.org scan antenicenefathers01robe.pdf, PDF with text layer; S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.T. Otto, vol. 1, Jena: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1)
what_it_says: Justin names the Father, the Son who taught the Christians, the host of angels and the prophetic Spirit together as the objects of worship.
limits: Worship of the Son and Spirit is named, but the Spirit is not called God here and no homoousios; the 'Son' is 'came forth from Him'.

ref: 1 Apol. 13.3-4 (Otto section 13; ANF ch. XIII 'Christians serve God rationally')
greek: υἱὸν αὐτοῦ τοῦ ὄντως Θεοῦ μαθόντες καὶ ἐν δευτέρᾳ χώρᾳ ἔχοντες, πνεῦμά τε προφητικὸν ἐν τρίτῃ τάξει ὅτι μετὰ λόγου τιμῶμεν, ἀποδείξομεν. Ἐνταῦθα γὰρ μανίαν ἡμῶν καταφαίνονται, δευτέραν χώραν μετὰ τὸν ἄτρεπτον καὶ ἀεὶ ὄντα Θεὸν καὶ γεννήτορα τὸν ἁπάντων ἀνθρώπῳ σταυρωθέντι διδόναι ἡμᾶς λέγοντες, ἀγνοοῦντες τὸ ἐν τούτῳ μυστήριον, ᾧ προσέχειν ὑμᾶς ἐξηγουμένων ἡμῶν προτρεπόμεθα.

english: ...that we reasonably worship Him, having learned that He is the Son of the true God Himself, and holding Him in the second place, and the prophetic Spirit in the third, we will prove. For they proclaim our madness to consist in this, that we give to a crucified man a place second to the unchangeable and eternal God, the Creator of all
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1)
page: ANF printed p.166-167 (PDF 184-185; p.167 verified as printed number on PDF p.185); Otto printed p.164 (PDF 244, verified)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (1885-96), ed. Roberts & Donaldson; archive.org scan antenicenefathers01robe.pdf, PDF with text layer; S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.T. Otto, vol. 1, Jena: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1)
what_it_says: Justin says Christians hold the Son second and the prophetic Spirit third, and that worshipping the crucified Christ as second to God is not madness.

ref: 1 Apol. 32 (ANF ch. XXXII 'Christ predicted by Moses'; Otto section 32)

ref: 1 Apol. 46.2 (Otto section 46; ANF ch. XLVI 'The Word in the world before Christ')

ref: 2 Apol. 6 (ANF ch. VI 'Names of God and of Christ, their meaning and power')

Ὁ δὲ Υἱὸς ἐκείνου, ὁ μόνος λεγόμενος κυρίως Υἱὸς, ὁ Λόγος πρὸ τῶν ποιημάτων, καὶ συνὼν καὶ γεννώμενος, ὅτε τὴν ἀρχὴν δι᾽ αὐτοῦ πάντα ἔκτισε καὶ ἐκόσμησε
greek_edition: Migne PG 6, Paris 1857 (archive.org patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_006_justin_et_al_version1; Google scan, OCR): OCR only, column unknown; OCR errors likely ('πρεσδύτερην', 'εὐποιΐτῶν', 'κτίστης' spelling). Not checked against Otto vol. 1 (Otto p. for 2 Apol. not located).

page: ANF printed p.190 (PDF 208, inferred); Migne PG 6 page unknown

ref: 2 Apol. 10 (ANF ch. X 'Christ compared with Socrates')

For whatever either lawgivers or philosophers uttered well, they elaborated by finding and contemplating some part of the

ref: Dial. 56.4 (ANF ch. LVI 'God who appeared to Moses is distinguished from God the Father')
greek: καὶ τῷ Ἰαχὼδ, καὶ τῷ Μωσεῖ ὥφθαι λεγόμενος καὶ γεγραμμένος Θεὸς, ἕτερός ἐστι τοῦ πάντα ποιήσαντος θεοῦ, ἀριθμῷ λέγω, ἀλλὰ οὐ γνώμῃ. Οὐδὲν γάρ φημι αὐτὸν πεπραχέναι ποτὲ, ἢ ὅπερ αὐτὸν ὁ τὸν κόσμον ποιήσας, ὑπὲρ ὃν ἄλλος οὐκ ἔστι θεὸς, βεδούληται καὶ πρᾶξαι καὶ ὁμιλῆσαι.
greek_edition: Migne PG 6, Paris 1857 (archive.org patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_006_justin_et_al_version1; Google scan, OCR): OCR only; Migne 'βεδούληται' probably OCR for βεβούληται; 'Ἰαχὼδ' for Ἰακώβ as printed. Otto vol. 2 (Dialogue) not downloaded (70 MB).
english: ...that He who is said to have appeared to Abraham, and to Jacob, and to Moses, and who is called God, is distinct from Him who made all things — numerically, I mean, not [distinct] in will. For I affirm that He has never at any time done anything which He who made the world— above whom there is no other God — has not wished Him both to do and to engage Himself with.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1)
page: ANF printed p.223 (PDF 241; text layer reads 'merically', OCR error for 'numerically'); Migne PG 6 page unknown
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (1885-96), ed. Roberts & Donaldson; archive.org scan antenicenefathers01robe.pdf, PDF with text layer; Migne PG 6, Paris 1857 (archive.org patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_006_justin_et_al_version1; Google scan, OCR)
what_it_says: Justin says the God who appeared to Moses, Jacob and Abraham is another God, numerically distinct from the Maker of all but not different in will or purpose.
limits: This is the 'another God' (heteros theos) passage. Justin says 'numerically' distinct but 'not in will'; the Greek 'ἄλλος οὐκ ἔστι θεὸς' is said of the Maker, so it is a subordinationist text that Nicene readers answer by the unity of will and by the Logos' eternal relation, which Justin does not spell out.

ref: Dial. 61.1 (ANF ch. LXI 'Wisdom is begotten of the Father, as fire from fire')
greek: Μαρτύριον δὲ καὶ ἄλλο ὑμῖν, ὦ φίλοι, ἔφην, ἀπὸ τῶν Γραφῶν δώσω, ὅτι ἀρχὴν πρὸ πάντων τῶν κτισμάτων ὁ Θεὸς γεγέννηκε δύναμίν τινα ἐξ ἑαυτοῦ λογικὴν, ἥτις καὶ δόξα Κυρίου ὑπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου καλεῖται, ποτὲ δὲ Υἱὸς, ποτὲ δὲ Σοφία, ποτὲ δὲ Ἄγγελος, ποτὲ δὲ Θεὸς, ποτὲ δὲ Κύριος καὶ Λόγος· Ἔχειν γὰρ πάντα προσονομάζεσθαι ἔκ τε τοῦ ὑπηρετεῖν τῷ πατρικῷ βουλήματι, καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ Πατρὸς θελήσει γεγενῆσθαι.

english: I shall give you another testimony, my friends, from the Scriptures, that God begot before all creatures a Beginning, [who was] a certain rational power [proceeding] from Himself, who is called by the Holy Spirit, now the Glory of the Lord, now the Son, again Wisdom, again an Angel, then God, and then Lord and Logos; ... since He ministers to the Father's will, and since He was begotten of the Father by an act of will

what_it_says: Justin says God begot before all creatures a rational power from himself, called Glory, Son, Wisdom, Angel, God and Lord, begotten by an act of the Father's will.

greek: ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀριθμῷ ἕτερόν τί ἐστι, καὶ ἐν τοῖς προειρημένοις διὰ βραχέων τὸν λόγον ἐξέτασα, εἰπὼν τὴν δύναμιν ταύτην γεγεννῆσθαι ἀπὸ τοῦ Πατρὸς, δυνάμει καὶ βουλῇ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ᾽ οὐ κατὰ ἀποτομήν

translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (1885-96), ed. Roberts & Donaldson; archive.org scan antenicenefathers01robe.pdf, PDF with text layer; Migne PG 6, Paris 1857 (archive.org patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_006_justin_et_al_version1; Google scan, OCR)
what_it_says: Justin says the power was begotten from the Father by his power and will, not by division of his substance, and is numerically distinct.
